chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked him about a man performing tamattuʿ who had intercourse with his wife and had not yet trimmed his hair; he said:
"He must slaughter a camel, and I have feared that his hajj may have been impaired if he was knowledgeable; but if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him."

He said: And I said to him, about a person performing tamattuʿ who clipped some of his nails with his teeth and took some of his hair with a sharp tool. So he said: "There is no harm in it; not everyone finds scissors."

key_terms.ثُلِمَ حَجُّهُ: his hajj was damaged or impaired
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: acting in ignorance of the ruling
key_terms.عَالِمًا: acting with knowledge of the ruling
key_terms.يَنْحَرُ جَزُورًا: he must slaughter a camel as expiation
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْ: perform taqsir, i.e. trim the hair to exit ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamattiʿ who has intercourse before taqsir or trims hair and nails without scissors?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings concerning the mutamattiʿ after ʿUmrah al-tamattuʿ and before completing the acts of release from ihram. It states that intercourse before taqsir requires slaughtering a camel, with a warning of serious harm to the hajj if done knowingly, while the ignorant person bears no liability; it also permits cutting nails with the teeth and trimming hair with a sharp instrument when scissors are unavailable.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2745 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man performing tamattu‘ who had intercourse with his wife before trimming his hair.
Imam (as) said: "He must slaughter a camel. I fear that his Hajj may be invalid if he acted knowingly. However, if he acted out of ignorance, there is no penalty upon him."

Mu'awiyah also said: I asked him about a person performing tamattu‘ who bites their nails with their teeth or trims their hair using a sharp-edged tool.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it. Not everyone has access to scissors."
